status: HYPOTHESIS BACKLOG AND PLAN. Nothing in this file is a finding. No test in it has been executed; every result is 'not tested'. Retained existing tests are evidence from their own earlier runs. Failure to reproduce would not be proof of safety. No production-readiness claim.
source: External brainstorm of 75 attack hypotheses and 8 chains (ChatGPT); the 5 Oct 2026 recommendations are historical and were checked against current code only by reading it

classification_vocabulary.CAP: needs a capability that does not exist

scoring_note: priority_score = reach + capability + consequence (1-3 each, planning judgement) + evidence gap (covered 1, partial 2, not covered or capability missing 3, not applicable 0). A planning heuristic, not a severity assessment.

commits.pin: not pinned (read at 3cb0699e; main now ab3c14f1)

ideas.title: Alternate execution path
ideas.entry: Inventory of destination call sites (SCN-D09 ROUTES): CP BoundedAuthorizationWorkflow.execute; RT LocalDestinationExecutor.execute_snapshot, ControlPlaneRefundDestinationAdapter.apply, AtomicLocalControlPlaneExecutor.execute, IntentRefundDestination.commit; direct destination.commit; acp run and other CLIs; reaper thread; legacy AgentEngine and CLI
ideas.gap: Direct commit, snapshot execution and adapter apply are refused on effective-grant and atomic destinations, and the call-site list is checked against the source. By design a base destination holds no authority state and accepts a direct commit; raw SQL by the file holder and the OpenShell destination are out of model or unexercised. The call-site table was checked at the V1 pins; runtime fc034d14 added delayed-commit and operation-key destinations that the table does not name. No non-dispatching entry (reaper, recovery, import, CLI) has an unchanged-destination assertion.
ideas.known_limit: base destination and raw SQL holder are out of model (SCN-D09)

ideas.title: Payload substitution
ideas.entry: Routes A/B/C: approved proposal -> execution envelope or claim -> destination row (RT FrozenOperation, 23 members; CP AuthorizationBinding)
ideas.gap: Amount, target and envelope substitution are asserted; one-member-at-a-time completeness over every frozen-operation member and nested payload key is not, so an unbound member would not be noticed.

ideas.title: Cross-context authorization replay
ideas.entry: Routes A/B/C: tenant, actor, principal, institution, authority domain, manifest, run, environment, action type
ideas.gap: Tenant, actor, principal, institution, domain, manifest and environment are exercised. No table says which dimensions the authorization binds; run_id and correlation_id are bound only through the proposal commitment and are not perturbed.

ideas.title: Canonicalization disagreement
ideas.entry: acp run JSON ingress (cli_run._load_json uses json.loads: last duplicate member wins, NaN accepted before model validation); CP commitment (sort_keys, allow_nan=False); RT _canonical; verifier canon and strict wire parser
ideas.gap: Strict parsing is proven for the verifier, the deployment review and the pack importer, which are not on the decision path. No test feeds duplicate keys, NFC/NFD text, number spellings or BOM/trailing data through the governed ingress and compares the approved commitment with the destination row. Code-reading lead, not a finding.

ideas.title: Unbound extension fields
ideas.entry: RuntimeProposal (pydantic default ignores extras; acp run refuses unknown top-level members); RT ExecutionOperation is a closed dataclass; ODES x- extensions are digested
ideas.gap: Top-level unknown members are refused at acp run and the runtime operation is closed. Free-form nested members (payload, risk_metadata) are committed; no test shows that no adapter reads anything outside the committed set.

ideas.title: Declaration promoted to permission
ideas.entry: Manifest requirements, supported-claim and ODES records versus the grant check at decide() and effect time
ideas.gap: Covered across the control plane, the exchange envelope and the orchestrator contracts. Residual: new declarative profile members (rule_revision, holder inventory, freshness) have no promotion probe of their own.

ideas.title: Forged approval in natural language
ideas.entry: Natural-language approval claims in lower-trust fields on routes A and C
ideas.gap: Text cannot manufacture a grant or an approval on routes A and C.

ideas.title: Target alias substitution
ideas.entry: Grant scope and target match (CP bounded.py exact membership; RT SafeLocalPolicy uses str.startswith on allowed prefixes); destination database path
ideas.gap: Filesystem alias of the destination database is covered. Equivalent spellings of a target (case, trailing separator, prefix extension such as acct-1 against acct-10) and a resolver-level alias remap after approval are not asserted; a resolver-backed alias destination does not exist in V1.

ideas.title: Adapter impersonation
ideas.entry: adapter_id compared in the binding (CP bounded.py, id string only); RT ControlPlaneRefundDestinationAdapter; OpenShell CLI digest check
ideas.gap: Id-level impersonation is refused. Substituting implementation, configuration or destination credentials behind an unchanged adapter id is a documented non-goal (E6; V1 core addendum GR-1853 defers adapter_digest). An offline test can only record detected-only through ledger verification; prevention needs adapter attestation, which does not exist.
ideas.known_limit: E6: binding compares adapter id, not code

ideas.title: Manifest or policy downgrade
ideas.entry: Manifest version/digest and policy digest checks at decision and effect time; opt-in rule-revision profile (CP rule_revision.py)
ideas.gap: In-place edits and unadopted digests are covered. An earlier adopted-then-superseded digest presented as current is not. Manifests carry digests, not signatures, so a validly signed older manifest has no V1 referent. R1 finding 1 (adapter dropped rule_revision_profile unless freshness is on) is being fixed in stream F1; the effect-time pin depends on it.

ideas.title: Evidence-to-instruction injection
ideas.entry: Retrieved text in payload, narrative and descriptor fields of routes A/C; manifest descriptions
ideas.gap: The stack treats text as data; no model is in the loop, so this shows that no code path interprets text, not that an agent would resist it. Placed in tier 2 because the brainstorm's tier list has no slot for group F.

ideas.title: Authority ABA
ideas.entry: Grant resolver (id + revision) -> effect_id = commitment(proposal, grant_id, grant_revision); RT authority_grants_v1 provisioning refuses an existing id whose revision/status differ
ideas.gap: No test or doc found for revoke-then-recreate with the same grant id or equivalent fields. effect_id is a pure function of grant id and revision, so an approval for the first grant can match a resolver-supplied replacement with the same id and revision; the revoked status in the runtime authority row is the only observable difference. Code-reading lead.

ideas.title: Revocation at each boundary
ideas.entry: Routes A/B/C; boundaries: decision, claim provisioning, dispatch, commit transaction. RT revocation_closeout sidecar for queued/executing items
ideas.gap: Covered with the linearization point recorded per route. There is no queue between approval and execution in V1, so the queueing boundary only exists in the opt-in revocation_closeout sidecar (RT test_o6_p1d_revocation_closeout.py). Default route A keeps the recorded C0 residual race.
ideas.known_limit: C0 check-to-commit race (SCN-C07, INCONCLUSIVE by design)

ideas.title: Approval withdrawal race
ideas.entry: Approval status row; claim provisioning; commit transaction; RT DelayedCommit pause points
ideas.gap: Queued work and already-issued claims are handled separately (claim provisioning test and paused-transaction test).

ideas.title: Critical evidence invalidation
ideas.entry: Evidence rows at decision, claim provisioning and inside the destination transaction
ideas.gap: Dependency invalidation reaches the executing path on route B and the effective-grant route.

ideas.title: Stale authorization cache
ideas.entry: CP runtime-authority profile: cached status, per-class max_status_age_seconds, reversible-class tolerance; hub resolver assurance reference
ideas.gap: Resolver-side logic is covered. The documented reversible-class tolerance (act on a cached active status inside the age bound) is not shown end to end against a destination that stays reachable after a revocation, and no real process or network partition exists (single host).
ideas.known_limit: reversible class tolerates bounded stale status by design

ideas.title: Non-atomic revalidation
ideas.entry: Route A default (C0: revalidate, then destination.apply) versus effective-grant destination and route B (check inside the commit transaction)
ideas.gap: Prevention (atomic routes) and detection-only (C0 default) are both asserted and kept distinct. Residual: the adapter route with the opt-in delayed-commit destination has not been mapped onto the same prevented/detected-only split.

ideas.title: Clock disagreement
ideas.entry: CP trusted clock, observation floors; RT destination _trusted_now inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE; ODES recipient clock; BitRep half-open intervals
ideas.gap: Per-evaluator boundaries are covered. Equality at the exact expiry instant and timezone-offset equivalence are not compared across the control plane, the destination transaction and the recipient on one fixture.

ideas.title: State rollback
ideas.entry: Restore of destination database, control-plane store, witness ledger and (opt-in) operation-key and budget tables
ideas.gap: Restore is characterised and prevention is blocked on an independently administered anchor (SCN-D07 INCONCLUSIVE). The programme-2 state added after that characterization (operation keys, effect budgets under the R2 key, freshness floors) has not been rolled back in a test. Prevention needs the external anchor, which does not exist.

ideas.title: Retry identity laundering
ideas.entry: Re-planned proposal (new effect_id) after an unresolved effect; opt-in refund-intent registry (route B only); operation identity (renewal only)
ideas.gap: Characterised, not prevented, on the default routes: logical-intent prevention is not implemented, adopted or qualified (hub logical-intent-prevention-contract); the intent profile cannot combine with route A (F-18); the default atomic route double-commits after renewal at cap 2 (orchestrator F-5, KNOWN GAP; opt-in key merged in runtime fc034d14). The full chain with a concurrent retry is not exercised.
ideas.known_limit: business-level duplication not prevented by default (F-5, F-18)

ideas.title: Concurrent duplicate delivery
ideas.entry: Same effect through several processes and entry points: routes A/B/C, exchange redelivery
ideas.gap: Covered per route. Mixed-route simultaneous delivery to one database is excluded by profile exclusivity rather than raced.

ideas.title: Idempotency-key collision
ideas.entry: effect_id/attempt_id/operation key uniqueness inside destination transactions
ideas.gap: Covered, including principal/domain scoping of the opt-in operation key.

ideas.title: Lost acknowledgement after commit
ideas.entry: Routes A/B/C; RT DelayedCommit destination (opt-in) and simulate=lost_ack
ideas.gap: Covered on all three routes and on the opt-in delayed-commit destination.

ideas.title: Crash at persistence boundaries
ideas.entry: Boundaries: claim persistence, dispatch, commit, result record, observation, refusal write; programme-2 journal, join-row, operation-key and witness writes
ideas.gap: Route B and the runtime use real process kill. Routes A and C use a BaseException crash model (SCN-C08 INCONCLUSIVE: no OS-level kill). The freshness gate refusal is three separate writes (X4 finding), and the programme-2 write points have no kill-at-boundary matrix.
ideas.known_limit: no OS-level kill on routes A and C (SCN-C08)

ideas.title: Stale worker after lease expiry
ideas.entry: CP freshness profile: check lease, deadline at opening, reaper, superseded-owner write refusal; RT delayed-commit pause points; hub generation fence (reference)
ideas.gap: Journal and dispatch gate are covered. A worker paused after the gate and resumed after takeover is stopped by effect-id dedupe, not by a destination-enforced fencing token; the N3 profile is same-host flock only and cross-host fencing is not built. Needs a fencing capability for prevention; offline test can measure detected-only.

ideas.title: Compensation abuse
ideas.entry: No compensation or rollback action exists; RT cancellation is not rollback; ODES effect-reversibility is a draft contract (#75)
ideas.gap: Needs a compensating-action capability (a refund-reversal action with its own grant), which does not exist; adjacent recovery paths are shown not to dispatch. Retained tests prove only that no reversal is claimed.

ideas.title: Policy-change injection
ideas.entry: Rule-revision profile (opt-in) and policy digest; adoption flow of SCN-C20 is unimplemented (decision D9)
ideas.gap: Digest and chain checks stop an edited policy; an observed outcome presented as already adopted policy is not run through an adoption flow because SCN-C20 policy adoption is unimplemented (D9).

ideas.title: Partial batch execution
ideas.entry: Route B multi-part composition (claims on a shared budget); route C partial delivery successor
ideas.gap: Covered for composed parts. The reference has no native multi-part operation (SCN-D05 INCONCLUSIVE), so batch semantics are exercised through parts on a shared budget.

ideas.title: Observation substitution
ideas.entry: Observation fields: effect, target, tenant, amount, interval
ideas.gap: Identity and payload substitution are caught; tenant, target and time-interval substitution of an otherwise genuine observation are not enumerated field by field.

ideas.title: Shared producer and observer compromise
ideas.entry: Executor identity and writable store reused to forge readback; HMAC export
ideas.gap: Needs an independently operated observer with its own credentials and storage, which does not exist in V1; the stack documents that producer and verifier share a trust domain, and tests assert the labelling, not prevention.

ideas.title: Caller-selected verification key
ideas.entry: BitRep verify with trust snapshot; Index API link route; Index chain adapter
ideas.gap: Forged and caller-keyed attestations are refused at the verifier, the Index link route and the control plane, with a no-snapshot fail-closed case and detector calibration controls.

ideas.title: Scope loss during summarization
ideas.entry: Exchange handoff and export, replay and ODES adapters (the only summarising steps in V1)
ideas.gap: Lineage and uncertainty survive export and known losses are enumerated. Restriction, expiry and approval-condition loss across a handoff are not asserted member by member; LLM summaries are not in V1 (decision D6).

ideas.title: Executor acknowledgement as observation
ideas.entry: Executor ack versus destination read; replay import report; verifier
ideas.gap: An ack without destination change does not become observed or verified; the effect oracle reads destination state independently.

ideas.title: Missing failures in export
ideas.entry: Replay export, evidence pack, ODES export, verifier ledger
ideas.gap: Dropped refusals and failures are detected where a prior witness digest exists; without a published digest the drop is accepted today and recorded as such (witness test, opt-in profile).
ideas.known_limit: dropped entry accepted without a published digest

ideas.title: Count and coverage manipulation
ideas.entry: Evidence pack totals, duplicate records, selective subsets against a source population
ideas.gap: Refusal-count relabelling and planted defects are detected; a pack claiming complete coverage without reconciling its source population is not tested as such, and copied-evidence packs carry the D14 limit.

ideas.title: Replay that causes effects
ideas.entry: Bundle open, import and verify paths; active references in bundles
ideas.gap: Reading and importing do not reach a destination at the pinned revisions. Programme-2 additions (reaper, recovery, new importers) lack an unchanged-destination assertion; T02 extends it.

ideas.title: Signed-content substitution
ideas.entry: BitRep wire parser and signature scope; verifier strict wire
ideas.gap: Subject, statement and framing alterations outside the signed portion are rejected before verification; digest-only integrity is labelled as not authentication.

ideas.title: Accepted-claim mutation
ideas.entry: Index claims service and API: update, delete, supersede; storage adapters
ideas.gap: Exposed API and service paths refuse rewrite and delete. Direct database edits by the storage holder are outside the model and are not claimed.

ideas.title: Contradiction suppression
ideas.entry: Index API list_evidence(limit, offset), filters, supersession links, chain adapter ordering
ideas.gap: History order and supersession terminality are covered. The relying view under pagination, offset and filter changes is not: list_evidence has limit/offset and no test found exercises a conflict dropping out of a page. Code-reading lead.

ideas.title: Fresh wrapper around stale evidence
ideas.entry: CP observation timestamps and staleness window; BitRep statement expiry; ODES recipient clock
ideas.gap: The observation time, not the envelope time, controls reliance on the control plane path.

ideas.title: Readback ambiguity
ideas.entry: Destination readback matching state created by another actor
ideas.gap: An effect without a consumed claim is flagged; matching state from another actor is attributed only through effect identity.

ideas.title: Lossy adapter transformation
ideas.entry: Producer record to replay to evidence pack to ODES round trip
ideas.gap: Unknown, absent and redacted do not collapse into success in the enumerated cases; profile-on records are refused by replay (F-4) and verifier (F-3), so the programme-2 shapes are not round-tripped.
ideas.known_limit: replay (F-4) and verifier (F-3) refuse profile-on records

ideas.title: HMAC mistaken for independent attestation
ideas.entry: Replay export HMAC; pack and ODES surfacing of authentication
ideas.gap: A holder of the shared secret can forge a record and the stack labels the HMAC as non-independent. Residual: documentation that mentions an HMAC key that does not exist (R1 finding 5, fix in stream F1).

ideas.title: Schema validity promoted to assurance
ideas.entry: ODES validators, replay importer, pack, verifier
ideas.gap: Structurally valid records claiming approval or completion are not promoted.

ideas.title: Evidence importer resource abuse
ideas.entry: Wire budget, nesting and cycle limits in hub, verifier wire and importers
ideas.gap: Limits are tested in the hub wire budget and verifier wire parser. Replay and ODES importer limit parity and compressed inputs were not mapped, and nothing was run.

ideas.title: Revoked-key temporal ambiguity
ideas.entry: BitRep key registry and trust snapshot currency; documented temporal semantics
ideas.gap: Historical verification and current reliance are separated and documented. Residual: no test shows an old valid signature cannot be reused as present authority by a consumer that ignores the snapshot, which is outside the Index and control-plane paths.

ideas.title: Evidence multiplication
ideas.entry: Index API and chain adapter corroboration computation
ideas.gap: Covered, and this is a reproduced known limit rather than a pass: the Index API cannot see copy provenance outside its own content-equality check (F-19; decision D14, SCN-C04 reproduces it). Result at the pinned revisions is a recorded failure, not safety.

ideas.title: Demonstration proof acceptance
ideas.entry: BitRep zero-knowledge demonstration artifacts and the assurance HTTP path
ideas.gap: Demonstration artifacts never verify and cannot carry assurance.

ideas.title: Redaction and signing confusion
ideas.entry: Sign-then-redact, redact-then-sign, manual redaction, derived files
ideas.gap: Each ordering has an asserted outcome.

ideas.title: Network destination escape
ideas.entry: Needs an egress-controlled executor; V1 reference engine has no network imports and a synthetic SQLite destination
ideas.gap: Needs a live OpenShell sandbox with a network policy (pinned gateway, Docker, immutable image; W6 blocked) or another egress-controlled executor. The retained live test requires that environment and is not part of the bounded Linux reference.

ideas.title: Child-process privilege inheritance
ideas.entry: Needs a sandboxed tool executor; the reference engine launches no child process
ideas.gap: Needs a tool executor that can spawn children under a sandbox (live OpenShell). Today only the absence of process and network use in the engine is asserted.

ideas.title: Process argument confusion
ideas.entry: The only subprocess site: RT OpenShell CLI adapter (constant argv, payload on stdin); legacy CLI statically asserted to reach no destination
ideas.gap: The one process-spawning adapter uses constant argv with the payload on stdin (mock transport). The live OpenShell gateway, image and CLI are not executed (W6 blocked), so option or shell injection through the real CLI is untested.

ideas.title: Credential scope mismatch
ideas.entry: Route A credential table / effective-grant row; route B claim scope; destination transaction checks of tenant, grant, operation
ideas.gap: Scope checks at the synthetic destination are covered and the local-credential-holder bypass is characterised (SCN-C11 INCONCLUSIVE: no credential broker). Real executor credentials for another tenant/resource/operation/environment need a credential broker, which does not exist; the hub protected destination is a reference profile.

ideas.title: Credential exposure through artifacts
ideas.entry: Every produced file, log line, exception text, stderr, replay export, evidence pack, ODES package, acp run envelope; subprocess environment
ideas.gap: Covered for the pinned profile artifacts. Not covered: the programme-2 profile artifacts (identity, freshness, rule revision, witness, holder inventory), the acp run stderr path that echoes untrusted member names (R1 finding 9, fix in stream F1), and encodings (base64, hex, JSON-escaped) of a seeded secret.

ideas.title: Isolation fallback
ideas.entry: Missing sandbox, authority tables, profile, trusted clock or registry; test-time flags (allow_test_time, --now); adapter profile forwarding
ideas.gap: Individual fail-closed cases are covered. There is no systematic enumeration of silent fallbacks: R1 finding 1 showed an adapter dropping the rule_revision_profile unless freshness was on, which is exactly a silent downgrade, and no generic profile-forwarding completeness test exists.

ideas.title: Filesystem boundary escape
ideas.entry: RT DurableRefundDestination path checks; CP acp run input/output confinement; record-store ids
ideas.gap: Traversal, symlink and dangling-link cases are covered; symlink swap after construction and hard links are characterised as declared out of model. Platform-specific path interpretation is not tested: Linux only (decision D2).
ideas.known_limit: symlink swap after construction and hard link out of model (SCN-C10)

ideas.title: Shared-budget race
ideas.entry: Route B budget table in the claim transaction; route A grant cap; route C (drives route A)
ideas.gap: Route B is covered with threads and processes. Route A and C last-unit races are characterised as a caller-supplied boundary and have no deterministic barrier test; the opt-in R2 atomic-route operation key changes the cap-2 outcome and needs its own last-unit case.

ideas.title: Aggregate-limit evasion
ideas.entry: Per-grant cap (route A), per-budget claims (route B); no ceiling across grants, workers or time windows
ideas.gap: Within one grant or budget the cap holds; independent budgets are an explicitly declared boundary and no cross-grant aggregate ceiling exists, so grant multiplication is characterised, not prevented. Boundary test (T17) can measure it.

ideas.title: Delegation amplification
ideas.entry: CP refuses parent_grant_id (delegation_profile_unsupported); route B handoff of claims only
ideas.gap: Needs delegation support in the control plane (parent grant, narrowing rules, redelegation rights), which does not exist; today delegation requests are refused and the refusal is tested.

ideas.title: Cancellation propagation gap
ideas.entry: No parent/child task graph or scheduled follow-ups; single-run cancellation ordering only
ideas.gap: Needs a task graph with parent and child runs, retries and scheduled follow-ups; V1 has none (no merge or queue concept). Only single-run cancellation ordering is tested.

ideas.title: Fleet suspension gap
ideas.entry: Fleet suspension scenario SCN-C19 is unimplemented (decision D9); revocation closeout sidecar is per item
ideas.gap: Needs fleet-level suspension with partition and restart of a worker holding credentials and queued work (SCN-C19, unimplemented, D9). The retained test shows only per-run revocation.

ideas.title: Cross-tenant orchestration collision
ideas.entry: Task ids, claim ids, budget ids, run-record ids, cache keys and workspace paths across synthetic tenants
ideas.gap: Tenant substitution and scoped operation keys are covered; identifier reuse of budget ids, run ids and workspace paths across tenants is not enumerated.

ideas.title: Delegated-agent authority laundering
ideas.entry: Route C informational messages; route B handoff of claims between agents
ideas.gap: A completion or approval message from another agent carries no authority on routes B and C; delegation proper is unsupported (see G49).

ideas.title: Restart as renewed authority
ideas.entry: Process restart, reopened stores, saved run records, claim reuse after expiry
ideas.gap: Authority is recomputed from stores after restart; saved conversation or agent context is not part of V1 (decision D6), so only store-backed restart is covered.

ideas.title: Availability pressure on governance
ideas.entry: Unauthenticated flood on CP, exchange and admission; hold claims; reaper; timeout paths
ideas.gap: Floods do not weaken effect or evidence gates, within bounded fixtures. No review queue, ingress rate limiter or emergency path exists, so timeout and overload paths that could weaken authorization cannot be exercised; reaper thread death is silent (R1 finding 6).

ideas.title: Memory poisoning
ideas.entry: Governed memory is out of V1 scope (decision D6)
ideas.gap: Not applicable to V1: governed memory was moved out of scope by decision D6. Preserved as a hypothesis for any later memory profile; hub context_memory_profile tests exist but are not part of the V1 claim.

ideas.title: Compromised evidence producer
ideas.entry: Test runner or adapter fabricating observations and a passing report
ideas.gap: Seeded defects and retained test identities give partial detection. An independent producer of evidence for the same run does not exist (CI and suite share one trust domain); the verifier-mutation suite tests detection power, not an adversarial producer.
ideas.known_limit: single trust domain for runner and evidence

ideas.title: Artifact swap after verification
ideas.entry: Pin check at install and import; OpenShell CLI digest; component checkout verification
ideas.gap: Drift before use is refused. A swap between verification and load (time-of-check to time-of-use) is not exercised; owned by the deferred supply-chain stream (S3).

ideas.title: Qualification evidence substitution
ideas.entry: Dashboard accounting, release evidence packet, import of accepted revisions
ideas.gap: Relabelling and changed test bytes are detected. Results from another commit, fixture or workflow attempt are not systematically perturbed against the release evidence packet.

ideas.title: Skipped or mocked checks presented as coverage
ideas.entry: Scenario coverage map; test-symbol existence; evaluator sentinels
ideas.gap: Symbol existence and reduced-row accounting are checked. Nothing checks that a cited test asserts destination state, is not skipped, or mocks below the relevant boundary. T20 audits this for the batch citations.

ideas.title: Control-panel divergence
ideas.entry: Hub release-closeout control panel (md plus companion JSON), failure register, scenario report
ideas.gap: Dashboards are derived and refuse overclaims. The hub control panel is hand-edited markdown with a companion JSON and no test compares it with the failure register. Hub bytes are frozen, so a fix is a coordinator follow-up; a read-only checker can live here.

ideas.title: Mutable release reference
ideas.entry: Workflow pins by sha, hub component-lock, tag and branch use in release tooling
ideas.gap: Hashes are used for component pins. No test moves a tag or branch after qualification and observes the release tooling; owned by S3.

ideas.title: Dependency and profile mismatch
ideas.entry: Contract matrix, V1 profile pins, component lock, profile exclusivity
ideas.gap: Unsupported combinations are refused at the contract matrix and profile exclusivity. The opt-in programme-2 profiles are not yet in the matrix (registry changed 121 to 139 codes under an unchanged label, R1 finding 4).

ideas.title: Security exclusion abuse
ideas.entry: Security coverage tool exclusions and review scope
ideas.gap: Unreviewed classes are labelled as such. Broadening an exclusion or renaming a path while the dashboard stays green is not tested; owned by S3.

ideas.title: Cross-adapter semantic drift
ideas.entry: Same frozen request through native, OpenShell (mock), OpenAPPA and Microsoft AGT paths
ideas.gap: Optional OpenAPPA compatibility and comparative governance exist; the same frozen request has not been replayed across all adapters, the live OpenShell and Microsoft AGT paths are unavailable, and OpenAPPA is optional and not in the core lock.

chains.title: Malicious retrieved evidence, poisoned context, payload substitution, legitimate executor credentials
chains.note: Links are each covered (SCN-ASW-P01, SCN-D02, SCN-C11) but not composed. A composed test needs a payload that survives the injection stage and reaches a credentialed destination; T04 and T16 supply the substitution and credential legs. The context-poisoning stage has no model in V1.

chains.title: Revoked grant, stale cache, partitioned worker, late commit, misleading verified export
chains.note: Offline-testable as a single sequence on one host (revoke, cache-age, paused worker, late commit, export, verify) using the delayed-commit destination and the barrier pause points; T08 and T12 are its legs. A real partition needs a second host, which does not exist.

chains.title: Lost acknowledgement, new effect id, concurrent retry, duplicate business effect
chains.note: Characterised as a known limitation: default routes do not prevent a business-level duplicate (F-5, F-18). T11 runs the full chain per configuration (default, operation identity on, refund intent on route B).

chains.title: Copied attestations, inflated confidence, supported claim treated as authority, unauthorized action
chains.note: Offline-testable and expected to be refused at the last link: issue #42 records that the Index has no path into control-plane decisions, and SCN-C03 shows forged evidence never becomes authority. The copied-evidence step reproduces F-19 and the chain end-to-end is not run.

chains.title: Manifest downgrade, alternate adapter route, broader credentials, incomplete replay record
chains.note: Legs covered separately; the downgrade leg depends on R1 finding 1 (rule-revision forwarding) and the replay leg is refused for profile-on records (F-4). T19, T15 and T06 are the legs.

chains.title: Compromised executor, forged observation, evidence-pack transformation, false independent assurance
chains.note: Needs an independent observer to be preventable (capability absent); the transformation and labelling legs are covered. An offline run can only show what the stack labels, not that it detects.

chains.title: Child-agent delegation, aggregate-budget evasion, cancellation gap, continued effects after suspension
chains.note: Delegation, cancellation and fleet suspension do not exist; only the aggregate-budget leg (G47) is offline-testable.

chains.title: Passing qualification on one commit, mutable release reference, artifact substitution, false release readiness
chains.note: Pin and relabel checks exist; tag/branch movement and time-of-check swap are owned by the deferred supply-chain stream (S3).

batch_1.title: Direct-call matrix over every destination class
batch_1.cap: Holder of a destination object or database path who calls its public methods directly
batch_1.entry: Public commit, execute_snapshot and apply methods of each destination class at component mains, including the delayed-commit and operation-key destinations added after the SCN-D09 table
batch_1.inv: Without a valid effective-grant row and matching claim, no effect row appears, on every destination class that claims to enforce authority; a base destination that accepts the call is listed, not hidden
batch_1.fixture: Fresh store per destination class; one approved operation; call each public method with no grant, an expired grant, a revoked grant and a wrong-tenant grant
batch_1.expected: Refusal on every authority-enforcing class; destination row count read from the database file independently of the return value; base destination recorded as detected-only/not applicable by design
batch_1.pos: The same call with a valid grant commits exactly one row
batch_1.resid: Raw SQL by the database-file holder and live OpenShell remain out of model

batch_1.title: Non-dispatching entry points leave destinations unchanged
batch_1.cap: Any caller of reaper, recovery, replay import, evidence-pack, ODES and acp read-only commands
batch_1.entry: Reaper thread and sweeps, check-lease recovery, replay import, evidence-pack build, ODES export, acp witness and read-only commands
batch_1.inv: These paths never create, change or delete a destination row or a claim
batch_1.fixture: Destination with one landed effect and one unresolved attempt; hash every table and file before and after each entry point, including under a flood of malformed inputs
batch_1.expected: Destination hash unchanged for every entry point; reaper death is observed (R1 finding 6) and recorded as inconclusive if undetectable
batch_1.pos: A dispatching entry (execute) changes the hash, proving the observer can see change
batch_1.resid: New entry points added after this plan are not covered

batch_1.title: Raw-ingress canonicalization differential at acp run
batch_1.cap: Author of the JSON input file
batch_1.entry: cli_run._load_json (json.loads: last duplicate member wins, NaN accepted) into the proposal model, commitment and destination row
batch_1.inv: What was approved is byte-for-byte what the destination receives; duplicate keys, NaN or Infinity, BOM or trailing data, NFC against NFD text and number spellings (1, 1.0, 1e0) are refused or normalised identically on both sides
batch_1.fixture: One proposal file with a perturbation per case; run through acp run; compare the approved commitment with the stored operation
batch_1.expected: Refusal, or equal commitment and destination operation; any difference is a reproduced failure
batch_1.pos: Unperturbed file executes once with equal commitment
batch_1.resid: Other ingress formats and the library API are separate

batch_1.title: Every-field post-approval mutation completeness
batch_1.cap: Holder of the approved envelope or claim between decision and effect
batch_1.entry: Routes A, B and C; the 23-member FrozenOperation, AuthorizationBinding and the claim row
batch_1.inv: Mutating any single member or nested payload key after approval, including run_id and correlation_id, either changes the commitment and is refused, or is listed as unbound with the reason
batch_1.fixture: One approved operation per route; mutate each member in turn (generated from the model members so a new member forces a new case)
batch_1.expected: Refusal with no destination row for every bound member; unbound members listed explicitly
batch_1.pos: Unmutated operation executes once
batch_1.resid: Adapter-internal behaviour is not covered (see T06)

batch_1.title: Target equivalence and prefix semantics
batch_1.cap: Proposer choosing the target string
batch_1.entry: CP exact-membership target check (bounded.py) versus RT SafeLocalPolicy startswith on allowed prefixes
batch_1.inv: The two evaluators agree on which targets are allowed; a target that extends a prefix (acct-1 against acct-10), differs in case, separator, Unicode form or trailing space is refused by both or the difference is recorded
batch_1.fixture: Grant for one target; a table of equivalent and near-equivalent spellings evaluated on both routes
batch_1.expected: Same decision from both evaluators for every row; a disagreement is a reproduced failure
batch_1.pos: Exact target allowed on both
batch_1.resid: Resolver-level alias remap has no V1 referent

batch_1.title: Adapter identity versus implementation
batch_1.cap: Party who can replace adapter code or configuration behind an unchanged adapter id
batch_1.entry: Adapter id binding (CP) and ControlPlaneRefundDestinationAdapter; ledger verification
batch_1.inv: A swapped implementation under the same id is detected after the fact by the ledger, or the gap is recorded as accepted limit E6
batch_1.fixture: Registered adapter, then a lookalike class with the same id that writes a different amount
batch_1.expected: Result is detected only (ledger shows the mismatch) or reproduced failure; never recorded as prevented
batch_1.pos: Registered adapter yields a consistent ledger
batch_1.resid: Prevention needs adapter attestation (absent)

batch_1.title: Authority ABA
batch_1.cap: Administrator who revokes and recreates a grant with the same id
batch_1.entry: Grant resolver (id, revision), effect_id, RT provision_claim and authority_grants_v1
batch_1.inv: An approval or claim made against the first grant cannot spend authority of a re-created grant unless it is bound by revision and status; the provisioning refusal on differing rows holds
batch_1.fixture: Grant G rev 1 approved, revoked, recreated as G rev 1 (and rev 2) with identical fields; attempt execute on routes A and B
batch_1.expected: Refusal and no destination row, or reproduced failure documenting which field distinguishes the grants
batch_1.pos: Original grant executes once before revocation
batch_1.resid: Resolver implementations are external

batch_1.title: Revocation against the delayed-commit destination: prevented or detected only
batch_1.cap: Revoker acting at a chosen point of the commit sequence
batch_1.entry: Route A default (C0), effective-grant destination, route B, and the delayed-commit destination with its pause points
batch_1.inv: Per route, revocation placed before, inside and after the destination transaction is classified prevented or detected only and the classification matches the documented checkpoint level
batch_1.fixture: Deterministic barrier at each pause point; event order recorded; destination rows read independently
batch_1.expected: Prevented on atomic routes; detected only on default route A; any mismatch is a reproduced failure
batch_1.pos: No revocation yields exactly one effect
batch_1.resid: C0 race on default route A is by design

batch_1.title: Expiry equality and offset across evaluators
batch_1.cap: Proposer controlling timestamps and offsets
batch_1.entry: CP clock, destination _trusted_now, ODES recipient clock
batch_1.inv: At the exact expiry instant and with equivalent offsets (Z, +00:00, +01:00 shifted) all evaluators agree
batch_1.fixture: Grant and evidence expiring at T; evaluate at T-1us, T, T+1us with equivalent offsets on each evaluator
batch_1.expected: Identical accept or refuse decision per instant across evaluators
batch_1.pos: Mid-validity instant accepted by all
batch_1.resid: Real clock skew between hosts is not modelled

batch_1.title: Rollback of programme-2 state
batch_1.cap: Operator restoring a database or store from backup
batch_1.entry: Restore of operation-key table, effect budgets under the R2 key, freshness floors and witness ledger
batch_1.inv: After restoring an older copy, a spent operation key, budget unit or published witness digest is either still enforced or the loss is detected by a prior digest; undetected loss is recorded
batch_1.fixture: Spend a key and a budget unit, snapshot, spend again, restore the earlier snapshot, retry
batch_1.expected: Prevented, detected only (witness) or reproduced failure per table; SCN-D07 classification extended, not replaced
batch_1.pos: No restore gives the refusal
batch_1.resid: Prevention needs an external anchor (absent)

batch_1.title: C3 chain per configuration
batch_1.cap: Retrying client with a re-planned proposal
batch_1.entry: Lost ack, re-plan with new effect id, concurrent retry, on default, operation-identity-on and refund-intent routes
batch_1.inv: Count business-level effects per configuration; default configurations may duplicate (known), opt-in ones must not
batch_1.fixture: One business request; lost ack; second proposal with new effect_id; two concurrent submissions with a barrier
batch_1.expected: Effect count per configuration recorded from destination rows; default duplicate is recorded as reproduced known failure, not hidden
batch_1.pos: Single submission yields one effect
batch_1.resid: Logical-intent prevention is not implemented

batch_1.title: Stale worker resumes after lease or deadline expiry
batch_1.cap: Worker paused by the scheduler, resumed after takeover
batch_1.entry: Freshness profile gate, delayed-commit pause point, destination commit
batch_1.inv: A resumed worker whose lease has expired is refused at the destination or its effect is detected; no second effect
batch_1.fixture: Worker A pauses after the gate; lease expires; worker B takes over and commits; A resumes
batch_1.expected: Prevented by effect-id dedupe; the destination-enforced fencing absence recorded as residual
batch_1.pos: Without takeover A commits once
batch_1.resid: Same-host flock only; no cross-host fencing

batch_1.title: Real process kill at five write points of the route-A sequence
batch_1.cap: Operator or fault killing the process
batch_1.entry: Routes A and C (BaseException model today) and programme-2 write points: journal, join row, operation key, witness
batch_1.inv: After SIGKILL at each boundary and restart, destination holds at most one effect and no state claims success without it
batch_1.fixture: Subprocess killed at barrier N for each boundary; restart; read destination
batch_1.expected: At most one effect per boundary; any state that over- or under-claims is a reproduced failure
batch_1.pos: No kill yields one effect
batch_1.resid: Machine crash and fsync loss are not modelled

batch_1.title: Observation field matrix
batch_1.cap: Executor or party who writes observations
batch_1.entry: Replay import, verifier, effect oracle
batch_1.inv: A genuine observation with one field changed (effect, target, tenant, amount, interval) or a matching state written by another actor is never counted as verified completion
batch_1.fixture: One verified run; substitute each field in turn from another genuine run; add an unrelated matching row
batch_1.expected: Not verified for every substitution; ack-only run not verified
batch_1.pos: Unchanged observation yields verified
batch_1.resid: Verifier refuses profile-on records until J1 (F-3)

batch_1.title: Profile-flag forwarding completeness
batch_1.cap: Misconfiguration or older caller
batch_1.entry: Every adapter and executor constructor that accepts a profile flag
batch_1.inv: A profile set at the control plane is forwarded to every adapter and enforced at effect time, or construction fails; none is silently dropped
batch_1.fixture: Generate all combinations of rule-revision, freshness, operation-identity, witness, holder inventory flags
batch_1.expected: Flag effective or refusal at construction; silent drop is a reproduced failure (known: R1 finding 1)
batch_1.pos: All flags on yields all enforced
batch_1.resid: Fix is in stream F1; this test is its regression guard

batch_1.title: Canary-secret sweep over the work directory, executor result, Replay bundle, Evidence Pack, ODES package and verifier report
batch_1.cap: Reader of any produced file, log or exception
batch_1.entry: All outputs, including programme-2 profiles and acp run stderr
batch_1.inv: A seeded canary secret appears in no artifact in plain text, base64, hex or JSON-escaped form
batch_1.fixture: Canary as credential and in payload; run success, refusal and crash paths; scan
batch_1.expected: No occurrence; any hit is a reproduced failure
batch_1.pos: Scanner finds a canary planted deliberately
batch_1.resid: Subprocess environment of live OpenShell untested

batch_1.title: Last-unit budget race and grant multiplication
batch_1.cap: Several workers or one actor with several grants
batch_1.entry: Route C and adapter route last unit; route B budget; N grants of cap 1
batch_1.inv: Last unit is spent once under barriers; grant multiplication across N grants is measured and reported as characterised
batch_1.fixture: Barrier before the commit; two workers on the final unit; N grants splitting one prohibited total
batch_1.expected: One effect for last unit; aggregate for N grants recorded as detected-only or reproduced failure
batch_1.pos: Single worker spends the last unit once
batch_1.resid: No cross-grant ceiling exists

batch_1.entry: Hub release-closeout control panel (md and json), failure register, scenario report
